new_roles.title: Director, Quality GxP Vendor Management & Audit Programs
new_roles.description:
Description:

**The Company:**

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.
* Develop Vendor Management metrics, analyze vendor performance and compliance trends, and lead a periodic cross-functional vendor review that feeds into Quality Management Review.
* Ensure inspection readiness in the vendor management function and assist functional areas with readiness related to selection, qualification, management and oversight of their vendors.
* Evaluate and implement electronic vendor management systems, as applicable.

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* BS/BA in a life science or related field, or equivalent industry experience.
* 10+ years’ experience in the Pharmaceutical/Biotechnology industry, including at least 5 years leading vendor management/audit programs in a GxP environment.
* Expert knowledge of FDA, EMA, MHRA and ICH GxP regulations and guidelines, including ICH E6(R3) expectations for sponsor oversight of service providers.
* Strong GxP foundation associated with vendor oversight.
* Demonstrated experience planning and managing GxP vendor and internal audits, including follow up of audit responses and CAPAs.
* Experience developing and negotiating Quality Agreements with CROs, laboratories and other GxP service providers.
* Proficient with Veeva Systems, including Veeva Vault QualityDocs, desirable.
* Experience applying risk-based approaches to vendor tiering and oversight.
* Strong communication skills with all levels of the organization and external vendors, and the ability to influence functional areas without direct authority.
* Excellent organizational skills, analytical and problem-solving abilities, and strong verbal and writing skills.

**Benefits:**

Larimar Therapeutics offers all employees incentive stock options, a comprehensive benefits plan including 401K, and a flexible PTO policy.

***Equal Opportunity Employment***

*We are committed to equal-employment principles, and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live.*

*Employment policies and decisions on employment and promotion are based on merit, qualifications, performance, and business needs. The decisions and criteria governing the employment relationship with all employees are made in a non-discriminatory manner—without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical condition related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, military status, sexual orientation, or any other factor determined to be an unlawful basis for such decisions by federal, state, or local statutes.*

new_roles.title: Director, Quality Operations
new_roles.description:
**Revvity**

Revvity is a developer and provider of end-to-end solutions designed to help scientists, researchers, and clinicians solve the world’s greatest health challenges. We pair the enthusiasm of an industry disruptor with the experience of a longtime leader. Our team of 11,000+ colleagues from around the globe are vital to our success and the reason we’re able to push boundaries in pursuit of better human health.

Find your future at Revvity.

Our team is seeking a Director, Quality Operations to lead site quality for the Hopkinton-based operation. This role succeeds the current site quality leadership position and is intentionally scoped at the Director level because it combines broad operational accountability, organizational build-out, and a significant quality-system integration mandate. The Director will lead a blended Quality Operations organization spanning product quality, quality systems, supplier and incoming quality, inspection, and production support. The successful leader must protect ongoing product quality and compliance while progressively simplifying, integrating, and modernizing the operating model.

 
 

**Routine Responsibilities:**
-----------------------------

**Site Quality Leadership and Governance**
------------------------------------------

* Quality Operations leader for Hopkinton, with accountability for product quality, manufacturing quality, inspection, release, and site QMS execution.

* Provide visible, hands-on leadership in production and laboratory environments, enabling rapid risk-based decisions and timely escalation of material, process, product, and compliance issues.

* Own the site quality operating rhythm, including management review, quality metrics, risk review, resource prioritization, and cross-functional governance with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, R&D, Regulatory, Service, and Commercial teams.

* Serve as the principal site Quality representative for FDA, ISO, notified-body, customer, and internal audits, and ensure sustained inspection readiness across the blended operation.

* Balance product continuity, customer commitments, compliance, and transformation priorities using documented risk-based decisions.

 
 

**QMS, SOP, and Digital-System Integration**
--------------------------------------------

* Create and execute a phased roadmap improve and sustain SOPs and QMS structures supporting the site, with clear process ownership, sequencing, change controls, validation needs, and business-continuity safeguards.

* Optimize operating model for document control, production records, training, calibration, internal audits, supplier management, incoming inspection, final acceptance, complaints, and customer field interfaces.

* Lead the integration and modernization of quality tools and records currently distributed across systems and methods.

* Partner with enterprise Quality, Regulatory, IT/Digital, and business process owners to deploy scalable solutions and eliminate duplicate or conflicting workflows, records, and controls.

* Ensure data integrity, validated-state control, traceability, retention, access, and training are maintained throughout system and process transitions.

 
 

**Product and Manufacturing Quality**
-------------------------------------

* Lead quality support for a diverse portfolio that includes instruments, consumables and reagents platforms.

* Oversee incoming inspection, in-process controls, final product acceptance and release, nonconformance and material-review processes, manufacturing investigations, and CAPA effectiveness.

* Ensure appropriate validation and verification of manufacturing processes, equipment, software-enabled tools, inspection methods, and test methods.

* Drive preventive product-quality improvements using defect, yield, scrap, complaint, service, supplier, and Cost of Poor Quality trends.

* Represent Quality in design transfer, manufacturing transfer, new-product introduction, supplier changes, capacity expansion, and sustaining-engineering decisions.

 
 

**Organization Build and People Leadership**
--------------------------------------------

* Lead and develop a multi-disciplinary team of Quality Systems, Product Quality, Supplier/Incoming Quality, Quality Control, inspection, technician, and specialist roles.

* Implement planned organization expansion, including Quality Systems leadership, compliance coordination, QC supervision, and temporary integration support, while clarifying accountability across product and system responsibilities.

* Build succession depth and technical capability through coaching, performance management, role clarity, development plans, and targeted cross-training across legacy product and QMS environments.

* Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of ownership, constructive challenge, timely decision-making, and practical continuous improvement.

* Plan resource needs and manage the site Quality Operations budget, contractor usage, and external support in line with the operating plan.

 
 

**Customer, Supplier, and Compliance Interface**
------------------------------------------------

* Own the Quality Operations response to significant customer issues, quality agreements, customer audits, field escalations, and product-quality communications in partnership with Commercial Quality and Regulatory.

* Provide governance for supplier quality and incoming-quality activities, including risk-based controls, supplier corrective action, change assessment, and escalation of supply continuity risks.

* Ensure complaints, quality events, CAPAs, deviations, nonconformances, and risk-management activities are documented, investigated, assessed, and closed with appropriate rigor and timeliness.

* Responsible for customer complaint handling and investigations in collaboration with cross functional teams driving problem solving and resolution plans.

Maintain effective QMS training, document control, internal audit, calibration, and records-management programs across the site scope.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* bachelors degree
* 15+ years of quality experience with 7+ years management experience
 

 

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience supporting instruments, reagents and consumable product lines and systems.
* Experience deploying or consolidating eQMS, ERP, PLM, inspection, training, document-control, or calibration systems.
* Lean, Six Sigma, ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, or comparable credentials.
* Experience hosting regulatory and customer audits and managing complex customer-quality interfaces.
* Experience with data analysis, analytics, and management reporting schemes.
 

 

**Physical Requirements & Expectations:**

* The primary working condition associated with this position is working independently in the office environment.
* It is frequently required to work cross-functionally. Travel may be required up to 10%.
* Requires the ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds, sit and/or stand for prolonged periods of time and effectively manage conflict and emotional or stressful situations.
* Potential hazards associated with blood products.

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to the role.

 
 

**Compensation Range:**

The annual base salary range for this full-time position is $159,000 - $185,000. This range reflects the minimum and maximum target for a new hire in this position. The base pay actually offered to the successful candidate will take into account internal equity, work location, and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

Please note that base pay is only one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This range allows for the successful candidate to have an opportunity to progress within the position and develop at our company. This base pay range does not take into account bonuses, equity, or other benefits which may be applicable and are dependent on the level and position offered.

#LI-CH1

 
 
 

**What do we offer?**

We provide competitive and comprehensive benefits to our employees. Below are some highlights of our benefits:

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Options
* Life and Disability Insurance
* Paid Time-Off
* Parental Benefits
* Compassionate Care Leave
* 401k with Company Match
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan

Learn more about Revvity’s benefits by visiting our Bswift (opens in new window) page. Log-In instructions are provided towards the bottom of the Bswift page.

*For benefit-eligible roles only. Part-time and temporary roles may not be eligible for all benefits listed. Please reach out to your recruiter for more information.*

**Recruitment Scam Alert**

We've become aware that scammers are impersonating members of our recruitment team by using fake email addresses and fraudulent job opportunities.

Please remember:

We will never ask you to pay for an interview, job offer, equipment, training, or any part of our recruitment process. Always verify that recruitment emails come from our official company email domain (revvity.com). Revvity will never conduct interviews via text message, messaging apps, or social media direct messages. If you're ever unsure whether a recruitment message is genuine, please contact us through our official careers website before responding.
 
 
Your safety is important to us.
 
If you believe you've been targeted by recruitment fraud in the United States, you can report it to the Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) at https://www.ic3.gov/ or the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov .

new_roles.description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.
 + Proven ability to build and sustain positive relationships with diverse staff, families, and community. Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in education.
 + Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40pounds, and work indoors or outdoors.
 + Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity.
 + Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents in English.

Range of pay $34,216.00 - $80,000.00 Salary

**Our benefits meet you where you are.** We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life: 

* Know your whole family is supported with **discounted child care** benefits.

* Breathe easy with **medical, dental, and vision** benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
* Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with **employee assistance programs.**
* Feel great and thrive with access to **health and wellness programs, paid time off** and **discounts** for work necessities, such as cell phones.
* … and much more.

 
.

We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

*KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.*

new_roles.description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.
 + Proven ability to build and sustain positive relationships with diverse staff, families, and community. Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in education.
 + Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40pounds, and work indoors or outdoors.
 + Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity.
 + Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents in English.

**Our benefits meet you where you are.** We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life: 

* Know your whole family is supported with **discounted child care** benefits.

* Breathe easy with **medical, dental, and vision** benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
* Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with **employee assistance programs.**
* Feel great and thrive with access to **health and wellness programs, paid time off** and **discounts** for work necessities, such as cell phones.
* … and much more.

We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

*KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.*

new_roles.title: Director, RCM Vendor & Quality Management
new_roles.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

**About the Role**
------------------

The Director, Revenue Cycle Management provides strategic leadership across key Revenue Cycle functions, including outsourced operations and vendor management, credit balance management, and quality assurance. This role is accountable for improving financial and operational performance, strengthening controls, and ensuring internal teams and external partners consistently meet established service, quality, and compliance expectations.

 
 

You will partner across Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, and Training to improve cash and accounts receivable performance, resolve operational risks, and drive standardized, sustainable processes. This role provides leadership across multiple teams, vendors, and functional areas and translates organizational strategy into measurable operational goals and results.

 
 

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Lead Revenue Cycle operations and strategic support functions across areas such as patient access, business office operations, claims, accounts receivable, registration, insurance verification, payment and adjustment activities, and customer service.
* Provide governance and performance oversight for **third-party and BPO vendors**, including service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs), productivity, quality, contractual performance, issue escalation, and remediation.
* Lead **credit balance operations**, including identification, validation, refunds, adjustments, aging, resolution, root-cause analysis, and prevention of recurring patient and payer credit balances.
* Lead the **Revenue Cycle Quality Assurance program**, including quality standards, audit methodologies, sampling, scoring, performance reporting, corrective action plans, controls, and ongoing monitoring.
* Drive financial and operational performance across assigned Revenue Cycle functions, including cash, accounts receivable, operating expense, vendor spend, quality, compliance, customer experience, and productivity.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, Training, and external vendors to identify operational risks, resolve complex issues, standardize processes, and execute continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish governance, reporting, and escalation processes that identify performance gaps and support accountability, risk mitigation, root-cause analysis, and measurable improvement.

*Other duties may be assigned as needed to meet Company goals.*

 
 

**Basic Requirements**
----------------------

* **Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience.**
* Demonstrated professional experience in **Revenue Cycle Management or Revenue Cycle Operations**, including accounts receivable or related healthcare financial operations.
* Experience leading **third-party vendors, outsourced operations, or Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)** relationships, including vendor performance, SLAs, KPIs, or contract performance.
* Experience with **credit balance management**, including refunds, adjustments, resolution, aging, or related accounts receivable processes.
* Experience with **Revenue Cycle quality assurance, auditing, controls, or performance improvement**.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams and initiatives across complex or multi-site healthcare operations.
 

 

**Preferred Skills/Experience**
-------------------------------

* Experience leading Revenue Cycle functions across hospital, physician, infusion, or other healthcare environments.
* Demonstrated experience with root-cause analysis, process standardization, continuous improvement, risk mitigation, and corrective action planning.
* Strong ability to influence internal stakeholders and external partners and translate complex operational and financial information into actionable business decisions.
 

 
 

This position offers the possibility of a hybrid work arrangement based on recent updates to our in-office/work‑from‑home model. If located in DFW area, the selected candidate may be expected to work on‑site at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in‑office days may be designated according to team needs and business priorities.

We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets. The pay range shown below is aligned with McKesson's pay philosophy, and pay will always be compliant with any applicable regulations. In addition to base pay, other compensation, such as an annual bonus or long-term incentive opportunities may be offered. For more information regarding benefits at McKesson,

**Our Base Pay Range for this position**

$106,400 - $177,300

McKesson has become aware of online recruiting-related scams in which individuals who are not affiliated with or authorized by McKesson are using McKesson’s (or affiliated entities, like CoverMyMeds or RxCrossroads) name in fraudulent emails, job postings or social media messages. In light of these scams, please bear the following in mind:
 
 
McKesson Talent Advisors will never solicit money or credit card information in connection with a McKesson job application.

 

McKesson Talent Advisors do not communicate with candidates via online chatrooms or using email accounts such as Gmail or Hotmail. Note that McKesson does rely on a virtual assistant (Gia) for certain recruiting-related communications with candidates.

McKesson job postings are posted on our career site: careers.mckesson.com.

**McKesson is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

McKesson provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, age, genetic information, or any other legally protected category. For additional information on McKesson’s full Equal Employment Opportunity policies, visit our Equal Employment Opportunity page.

McKesson is committed to being an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and offers opportunities to all job seekers including job seekers with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to assist with your job search or application for employment, please contact us by sending an email to (United States) Disability\_Accommodation@McKesson.com or (Canada) Accessibility@mckesson.ca. Resumes or CVs submitted to this email box will not be accepted.

**Join us at McKesson!**

new_roles.title: Director, Quality
new_roles.description:
At Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company (EBAD), we believe that our strengths are built on our most important resource - our people. Join EBAD and you'll be a part of a team who creates cutting edge technology that will blast us into the future. No other company can match the innovative energetic solutions that we provide. At EBAD you will actively contribute to successful missions putting men, women and satellites into space, and protecting our armed service men and women around the world. If this is the culture and work environment you are seeking, then EBAD is the place for you!

**Job Description**

**Location:** Simsbury, CT

**Reports to:** VP of Operations

**Industry:** Aerospace & Defense

**Experience Level:** Director (15+ years)

**Shape the Future. Deliver Excellence. Achieve Zero Failure.**

At **Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense (EBAD),** we’ve been innovating for nearly **200 years,** delivering mission-critical technologies that protect lives and advance exploration. As we prepare to double in size over the next 3–5 years, we’re investing in our people and culture to support this transformation.

We’re seeking a dynamic **Director of Quality** to lead a complex, multi-site quality organization and drive performance at scale. Based at our headquarters in Simsbury, Connecticut, this role is critical to ensure the highest levels of product integrity, compliance, and customer trust across a rapidly growing business. This is not just about maintaining standards but about building a future-state vision for quality that enables growth, safeguards mission success, and strengthens EBAD’s reputation as a trusted partner.

**The Opportunity:**

EBAD’s customers depend on us to deliver our products with zero failure in mission-critical environments. The Director of Quality will be responsible for developing and executing a strategic Quality Management System (QMS) while leading quality operations across multiple sites. This leader will be tasked with driving measurable quality improvement, while also championing a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

This is an exciting opportunity for a leader to make an immediate impact by providing direction, driving the strategy for the business, and developing a problem-solving culture.

**Core Competencies for Success:**

* **Quality & Compliance Leadership:** Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries, with expertise in zero-failure mission environments.

* **Continuous Improvement & Performance:** Skilled in EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices with the ability to drive metrics-based improvement and systemic problem-solving.
* **Team Development & Leadership:** Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and build strong teams while fostering engagement and accountability.
* **Collaboration & Influence:** Strong cross-functional partnership with credibility to influence senior leadership, customers, and suppliers.
* **Resilience & Adaptability:** Able to manage ambiguity, drive change, and motivate teams in a fast-scaling environment.

**The Candidate We Are Looking For:**

* BS in an engineering discipline (MS preferred)
* Minimum 10 years of experience in high-mix, low-volume operations and manufacturing environment
* Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other mission-critical industries
* Demonstrated expertise in leading audits and managing compliance across regulatory bodies, customers, and suppliers, with deep knowledge of standards such as AS9100, ISO9001, and DoD requirements
* Proven ability to enhance customer quality by partnering closely with engineering, operations, and supply chain teams to consistently meet customer demand
* Strong record of measurable quality improvements
* Skilled in continuous improvement, performance metrics, and problem-solving through EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices
* Track record of building and developing strong teams, fostering high engagement, and driving accountability

**A Defining Leadership Opportunity:**

* **Legacy:** Join a privately held, 188-year-old business that takes a long-term approach, free from the short-term pressures of quarterly-driven reporting.
* **Impact:** Lead a mission-critical function where zero failure is the standard and success is business-defining.
* **Partnership:** Work directly with the BU President, senior leadership, and enterprise HR leaders in a highly influential role at the intersection of people and business strategy.
* **Culture of Excellence:** Help shape a culture that values people, integrity, and mission-driven excellence, driven by a Kaizen mindset and a commitment to quality and continuous improvement.

**Ready to Make a Difference?**

If you’re a proven quality engineering leader with the vision, discipline, and drive to achieve zero failure in a complex and growing business, this is your opportunity.

**Compensation and Rewards:**

We recognize that world-class leaders deliver world-class impact, and we reward accordingly. This role offers a competitive executive package that includes:

**Base Salary:** $175k – $225k plus annual bonus

**Executive Relocation:** Comprehensive support for a seamless transition

**Additional Enhancements:** Potential sign-on incentives and tailored rewards based on experience

*We offer a competitive compensation package aligned with skills & experience, with flexibility to reward top talent and extraordinary qualifications.*

*Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, national origin, or veteran status.*

new_roles.title: Director, Quality Compliance (Hybrid - Acton, MA)
new_roles.description:
Job Summary

The Director of Compliance provides strategic and operational leadership for critical compliance activities across the medical device organization. This role leads regulatory inspection readiness, product issue escalation and compliance risk assessment, regulatory agency responses, correction and removal activities, and large-scale compliance improvement initiatives.
 
 
The Director serves as a senior compliance partner to Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Operations, R&D, Supply Chain, and business leadership, ensuring significant quality and compliance issues are rapidly assessed, appropriately escalated, and effectively resolved. The position requires strong judgment, executive communication, and the ability to lead complex, cross-functional activities in a highly regulated environment.
 
 
Beyond compliance subject-matter leadership, the Director owns the compliance function's budget and resourcing, shapes its organizational strategy and structure, and contributes to broader business planning — balancing business objectives with compliance risk and representing the function in strategic and operational business reviews. The Director leads a global team of regional compliance specialists, building organizational capability across all manufacturing sites and functions.



**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

Organizational Strategy & Business Leadership

* Shape the multi-year strategy and organizational design for the compliance function, including workforce planning, capability building, and succession planning.

* Lead, develop, and manage a global team of compliance professionals, including direct oversight of regional compliance specialists across manufacturing sites.

* Partner with business, Quality, and Regulatory leadership to align compliance priorities with broader business strategy, product roadmaps, and operational plans.

* Represent the compliance organization in business planning, budget reviews, and strategic planning forums, providing a compliance-risk perspective to business decisions.

* Build organizational capability and structure to scale the compliance function as the business grows.

Inspection Readiness

* Establish and maintain an enterprise inspection-readiness program supporting regulatory inspections and other external assessments.

* Lead inspection preparation, including readiness assessments, mock inspections, documentation reviews, front-room/back-room preparation, subject-matter-expert coaching, and inspection logistics.

* Identify systemic readiness gaps and drive corrective actions to improve sustained inspection preparedness.

* Develop inspection-readiness metrics, lessons learned, and continuous-improvement mechanisms.

Product Issue Escalation & Risk Assessment

* Lead or facilitate cross-functional assessments of significant product quality, safety, compliance, and regulatory issues requiring senior-level escalation.

* Ensure emerging product issues are evaluated using structured, documented risk-based decision-making.

* Partner with Medical Safety, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Engineering, Operations, and other functions to evaluate product and compliance risk and determine appropriate escalation and response.

* Provide independent compliance challenge and guidance when significant product-related decisions could create regulatory or patient-safety implications.

* Ensure escalated issues have clear ownership, documented rationale, timely decisions, and appropriate executive visibility.

Regulatory Agency Responses

* Lead the development and coordination of responses to regulatory inspection observations, agency inquiries, compliance correspondence, and other significant regulatory matters.

* Establish cross-functional response teams, governance, deliverables, and escalation mechanisms.

* Ensure responses are factually supported, internally consistent, appropriately reviewed, and supported by sustainable corrective actions.

* Monitor commitments made to regulatory authorities through completion and verify appropriate evidence of implementation and effectiveness.

* Provide senior leadership with clear assessments of response status, risks, dependencies, and potential compliance exposure.

Correction & Removal Oversight and Execution

* Provide oversight and leadership for product corrections and removals, including recalls and field actions, in partnership with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Supply Chain, Commercial, and other relevant functions.

* Lead governance and execution for complex or high-risk correction and removal activities.

* Ensure decisions are supported by appropriate health-hazard, quality, regulatory, and compliance risk assessments.

* Establish clear accountability for affected-product identification, communications, execution, reconciliation, effectiveness monitoring, and closure.

* Monitor significant field actions through completion and escalate implementation risks or unexpected trends to senior leadership.

* Drive lessons learned and systemic improvements following significant product actions.

Large-Scale Compliance Improvement Projects

* Lead enterprise or multi-site compliance remediation and improvement programs involving significant regulatory, quality-system, or business risk.

* Translate regulatory observations, internal audit findings, systemic quality issues, or emerging compliance risks into structured remediation strategies and executable workstreams.

* Establish program governance, accountability, milestones, risk management, escalation processes, and executive reporting.

* Coordinate activities across functions and sites to ensure remediation addresses underlying systemic issues rather than isolated symptoms.

* Evaluate implementation progress and evidence of effectiveness to support sustainable closure.

* Serve as a compliance leader for major transformation initiatives involving quality-system processes, governance, controls, or organizational capabilities.

Leadership & Governance Responsibilities

* Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on significant compliance and regulatory risks.

* Provide independent compliance perspective during complex or high-risk decision-making.

* Establish governance mechanisms that enable timely escalation, transparent risk communication, and clear accountability.

* Develop organizational capability in inspection readiness, regulatory response, issue escalation, and compliance risk management.

* Promote a culture of proactive risk identification, regulatory accountability, patient safety, and sustainable compliance.

* Mentor and develop compliance professionals and cross-functional leaders involved in regulatory and remediation activities.

* Partner with business leadership on budget planning and resource allocation decisions affecting the compliance organization.

 

**Qualifications Required**
---------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, quality, regulatory affairs, or a related discipline and 12+ years’ industry experience.

* Significant progressive experience in Quality, Compliance, Regulatory Affairs, or related functions within the medical device or similarly regulated life-sciences industry.

* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading regulatory inspections and inspection readiness.

* Experience managing significant product quality or compliance escalations and structured risk assessments.

* Experience developing or coordinating responses to regulatory authorities.

* Strong working knowledge of medical-device quality-system and post-market regulatory requirements.

* Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional compliance or remediation programs.

* Experience managing budgets, resource planning, or organizational design within a compliance, quality, or regulatory function.

* Demonstrated business acumen, with the ability to balance business objectives and compliance risk in decision-making.

* Prior people leadership experience, including managing geographically distributed teams, strongly preferred.

* Strong executive communication, judgment, influence, and problem-solving skills.

 

**Core Competencies**
---------------------

* Regulatory and compliance strategy

* Organizational strategy and workforce planning

* Budget and resource management

* Business acumen and strategic planning

* Inspection management and readiness

* Product and compliance risk assessment

* Regulatory agency communication

* Correction and removal governance

* Quality-system remediation

* Program and project leadership

* Executive-level communication

* Cross-functional influence

* Critical decision-making under pressure

* Root-cause and systemic problem solving

* Change leadership

Additional Information:



Compensation & Benefits:

For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $172,400.00 - $258,575.00

This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
• Medical, dental, and vision insurance
• 401(k) with company match
• Paid time off (PTO)
• And additional employee wellness programs

Application Details:
This job posting will remain open until the position is filled.
To apply, please visit the Insulet Careers site and submit your application online.

Actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.
 
 
We are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. We do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. Our continued success depends on it!

At Insulet Corporation all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

( Know Your Rights )

new_roles.title: Director, Quality Center of Expertise – Design Quality
new_roles.description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 6 Dec 2026 
 

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

**A Day in the Life**
=====================

At Medtronic, you can begin a life-long career of exploration and innovation while helping champion healthcare access and equity for all. You'll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation in a more connected, compassionate world. We work with a sense of purpose and ownership, knowing there is a human life on the other side of every decision.
 
 
In this enterprise leadership role, the Director, Quality Center of Expertise (COE) – Design Quality will advance Design and Development excellence across Medtronic by shaping strategy, standards, governance, and enterprise capability for Design Quality and product development processes. Supporting every Medtronic Operating Unit and product category, this leader will drive consistency, strengthen Design Control execution, improve organizational capability, and help teams successfully navigate complex product development challenges.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings deep Design Quality and product development expertise, strong technical credibility, and a demonstrated track record of leading through complexity to deliver business, quality, and patient-focused outcomes. This individual will be a trusted enterprise partner who collaborates across Operating Units, Core Quality Services, and executive leadership teams to remove barriers, accelerate progress, and enable innovation while maintaining the highest standards of quality, compliance, and patient safety.
 
 
At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. In-person collaboration is critical to the success of this enterprise leadership role. This position requires an on-site presence a minimum of four days per week and must be based at one of the Medtronic U.S. campuses listed below. 

**Work Location**

This position will be onsite and based at one of the following Medtronic locations in the contiguous United States:

* Mounds View, MN / Minneapolis, MN (Twin Cities Campus)
* Irvine, CA / Santa Ana, CA (Orange County Campus)
* Lafayette, CO (Colorado Campus)
* Greater Boston Area (Boston, Danvers, or Mansfield, MA)
* North Haven, CT
* Memphis, TN
* Fort Worth, TX
* Jacksonville, FL
* Tempe, AZ

Travel up to 20% is required.

 

As **Director, Quality Center of Expertise (COE) – Design Quality** , you will provide enterprise leadership for Design Quality across Medtronic's global portfolio of medical technologies. You will partner with Operating Unit, Quality, Regulatory, Engineering, Product Development, and executive leaders to strengthen Design and Development practices, improve Design Control effectiveness, and enable successful execution across a diverse range of products and technologies.

You will serve as a highly credible Design Quality leader and trusted advisor, helping teams solve complex product development challenges while driving strategic initiatives that improve quality outcomes, product safety, regulatory readiness, and organizational performance.

Success in this role requires the ability to influence across a highly matrixed organization while maintaining a hands-on approach that removes barriers and accelerates execution. You will lead a small team of experts while driving enterprise-wide impact through collaboration, technical leadership, and capability building.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

 

***Lead enterprise Design Quality strategy, standards, and governance.***

* Develop and execute the enterprise Design Quality strategy, governance model, standards, and service priorities across Medtronic's global product portfolio.
* Establish and maintain enterprise Design Quality standards that enable consistent execution, regulatory readiness, and risk-based decision making.
* Own enterprise Design Quality process health, KPI visibility, and performance management mechanisms to identify trends, elevate risks, and drive timely action.
Create and lead governance mechanisms supporting critical product development programs, including escalation, issue resolution, and cross-functional decision making. 

***Drive enterprise initiatives and cross-functional partnerships that improve product development effectiveness, quality, and patient safety.***

* Partner with Operating Unit development teams to address complex design and development challenges through technical consultation, coaching, and expert guidance.
* Drive enterprise initiatives focused on improving product development effectiveness, product quality, patient safety, and risk management.
* Lead and influence strategic initiatives across the DRM Council, Productivity Workstream, Software Excellence Workstream, Global Operations & Supply Chain (GOSC), and Core Quality Services.
* Advance enterprise priorities, including Predicate Product Risk Reduction (PPRR) and other high-impact Design Quality improvement initiatives.
Partner with other Quality Centers of Excellence, including Risk Management, CAPA, and Acquisitions, to ensure alignment across critical quality processes. 

***Serve as the enterprise Design Quality expert, building capability and influencing critical decisions.***

* Serve as the enterprise subject matter expert for Design Quality, Design Controls, and Design & Development excellence.
* Build enterprise Design Quality capability through coaching, mentoring, talent development, and deployment of best practices.
* Influence decisions with potential enterprise-wide impact involving product safety, compliance, regulatory risk, legal exposure, business performance, and Medtronic's reputation.
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, technical excellence, continuous improvement, and patient focus. 

 

**Must Have: Minimum Requirements**

 

**To be considered for this role, please ensure the minimum requirements are evident on your resume.**

* Bachelor's degree required and 10+ years of relevant experience in Product Development, Design Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or related leadership roles **OR** Advanced degree with 8+ years of relevant experience in Product Development, Design Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or related leadership roles.
* Minimum of 7 years of people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading Design Quality and Design Control activities within regulated medical device, software, combination product, or similarly regulated industries.
* Demonstrated experience leading Design & Development, Design Quality, or Product Development initiatives across multiple business units, product platforms, or enterprise functions within a complex, matrixed organization.
Experience supporting the development, design transfer, or lifecycle management of regulated medical technologies. 

 

**Nice to Have**

 

***Product development and Design Quality experience across the lifecycle.***

* Extensive experience serving on product development Core Teams through multiple phases of the product lifecycle.
* Demonstrated success leading complex product development or Design Quality challenges across diverse technologies and product categories.
Experience leading enterprise-wide quality, product development, or transformation initiatives across multiple business units. 

***Deep technical, regulatory, and digital expertise.***

* Deep expertise in Design Controls, Design Verification and Validation, Risk Management, and Design & Development processes.
* Strong knowledge of FDA regulations, QMSR, ISO 13485, EU MDR, GMP, and other global regulatory requirements.
* Experience supporting software-enabled medical technologies, digital health products, combination products, or other complex regulated technologies.
Experience leveraging analytics, AI-enabled tools, automation, and digital technologies to improve quality performance and organizational effectiveness. 

***Leadership through influence in a highly matrixed environment.***

* Proven ability to build alignment and influence decision-making among technical experts, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.
* Demonstrated success leading through influence in a highly matrixed environment while delivering large-scale organizational impact.
* Hands-on leadership style with a demonstrated ability to remove barriers, accelerate execution, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

**Physical Job Requirements**

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position, but they are not an exhaustive list of all the required responsibilities and skills of this position.

The physical demands described within the Responsibilities section of this job description are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. For Office Roles: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer, and communicate with peers and co-workers. Contact your manager or local HR to understand the Work Conditions and Physical requirements that may be specific to each role.

**U.S. Work Authorization & Sponsorship**

At Medtronic, we are committed to fostering an environment where employees can thrive and make a meaningful impact. In alignment with our enterprise-wide workforce planning approach, U.S. work authorization sponsorship (H-1B, TN, J, etc.) is offered exclusively for Principal-level roles and above, where specialized expertise aligns with long-term business needs. Roles below the Principal level require candidates to possess unrestricted U.S. work authorization at the time of hire and for the duration of employment.
‌

**Recruitment Fraud Alert**

We are aware of phishing scams targeting job seekers. Please keep the following in mind:

 

Apply only through official Medtronic channels. All legitimate Medtronic recruiting communications come from approved Medtronic platforms and official @medtronic.com email addresses.

 

Medtronic will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information (such as bank account or Social Security details) during early stages of the hiring process. Any such requests are not legitimate.

 

If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Medtronic, do not respond, click links, or open attachments.

 

If you have any questions, concerns regarding the authenticity of a communication alleged to have been made by or on behalf of Medtronic, please contact us immediately at AskHR@medtronic.com .
‌

**Benefits & Compensation**
===========================

**Medtronic offers a competitive Salary and flexible Benefits Package** 
A commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values. We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help to create. We offer a wide range of benefits, resources, and competitive compensation plans designed to support you at every career and life stage.

Salary ranges for U.S (excl. PR) locations (USD):$184,000.00 - $276,000.00
‌ 
This position is eligible for a short-term incentive called the Medtronic Incentive Plan (MIP).The base salary range is applicable across the United States, excluding Puerto Rico and specific locations in California. The offered rate complies with federal and local regulations and may vary based on factors such as experience, certification/education, market conditions, and location. Compensation and benefits information pertains solely to candidates hired within the United States (local market compensation and benefits will apply for others).

The following benefits and additional compensation are available to those regular employees who work 20+ hours per week: Health, Dental and vision insurance , Health Savings Account , Healthcare Flexible Spending Account , Life insurance, Long-term disability leave , Dependent daycare spending account , Tuition assistance/reimbursement , and Simple Steps (global well-being program).

The following benefits and additional compensation are available to all regular employees: Incentive plans, 401(k) plan plus employer contribution and match , Short-term disability , Paid time off , Paid holidays , Employee Stock Purchase Plan , Employee Assistance Program , Non-qualified Retirement Plan Supplement (subject to IRS earning minimums) , and Capital Accumulation Plan (available to Vice Presidents and above, or subject to IRS earning minimums).

Regular employees are those who are not temporary, such as interns. Temporary employees are eligible for paid sick time, as required under applicable state law, and the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Please note some of the above benefits may not apply to workers in Puerto Rico.

Further details are available at the link below:

Medtronic benefits and compensation plans

It is the policy of Medtronic to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. In addition, Medtronic will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Medtronic will consider for employment qualified job applicants with arrest or conviction records in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality Assurance
new_roles.description:
**About CAMP Systems:** 
At CAMP Systems, we are the trusted leader in aircraft compliance and health management, proudly serving the global business aviation industry. With over 20,000 aircraft and 33,000 engines supported on our cutting-edge platforms, and partnerships with more than 1,300 maintenance facilities and parts suppliers worldwide, we’re shaping the future of aviation technology. Since our founding in 1968, we’ve grown to a dynamic team of 1,600+ employees across 14 locations globally—all united by a passion for innovation and excellence.

**Our Mission & Vision:** 
We connect the aviation industry through smart technology to make flight safer and more efficient, driving the future of aviation with intelligence and exceptional customer experiences.

**Our Values & Excellence Mindset:** 
We are customer obsessed, trust-driven, owners of our work, stronger together, constantly curious, and boldly innovative.

 

**What You Will Experience in This Role:**

The Director – Quality Assurance drives quality across CAMP's Aircraft Health Management business and provides quality oversight for data and process quality concerns. The role owns the QMS, the internal audit program, and the full quality escape lifecycle, and serves as CAMP's quality voice with OEMs, regulators, and key customers. The right candidate combines deep aviation maintenance knowledge with a disciplined, data-driven approach to compliance and continuous improvement.

This is a high-visibility leadership role reporting to the Vice President, Aviation Health Management Operations. The Director partners with senior leaders across a global organization and will build on an established quality program: strengthening the QMS, deepening OEM and customer confidence, and scaling quality practices as AHM grows.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Own and lead quality strategy across the full Aircraft Health Management organization, spanning maintenance tracking and engine health monitoring services, aligned with CAMP's business objectives.
* Serve as the escalation point for quality complaints from customer-facing, maintenance compliance, engine health monitoring, flight scheduling, and inventory functions.
* Partner with senior management and departmental leaders to embed quality methodologies across the organization and lead the associated change management.
* Own the quality budget, resource plan, and tooling (QMS, audit, and corrective action platforms), and build the succession pipeline for the quality team.

**Quality Management System & Certification**

* Own the Quality Management System (QMS) and quality SOPs, driving continuous improvement and ensuring processes meet strict regulatory and OEM requirements.
* Maintain ISO 9001 (or higher) certification for the engine health monitoring business, serving as external certification audit lead and ensuring ongoing audit readiness.
* Lead QMS management review with executive leadership, setting risk-based quality objectives and ensuring consistent QMS implementation (document control, competency records, data integrity) across all AHM locations in North America, Europe, and India.

**Audit & Compliance**

* Own the internal audit program end to end, including audit planning, execution, reporting, and the selection, training, and management of internal auditors.
* Host and manage OEM, customer, and third-party audits, driving findings to timely closure.

**Quality Escapes & Corrective Action**

* Manage all quality escapes from intake through investigation, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and verification of effectiveness, with clear accountability to customers and OEM partners.
* Define and report corrective action performance metrics (e.g., escape rate, time to containment, on-time closure, recurrence) with clear thresholds and escalation paths.

**OEM & Customer Engagement**

* Facilitate and chair weekly, monthly, and quarterly strategic OEM meetings covering quality trends, KPI compliance, and corrective action status.
* Serve as primary quality liaison to OEM partners, regulatory bodies, and high-profile customers and large fleet operators under significant OEM contracts.
* Facilitate weekly, monthly, and quarterly quality reviews with senior management and functional leaders, translating escape, audit, and customer feedback data into trends and strategic quality initiatives.

**Continuous Improvement & Team Leadership**

* Lead process improvement using Lean Six Sigma methods, mentoring teams and driving measurable reductions in escapes, rework, and risk.
* Maintain an executive quality scorecard (customer feedback, escapes, audit results, corrective action performance) to drive data-based decisions.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of four, setting priorities and fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and collaboration.
* Partner with AHM operations, training, and product leaders to ensure analyst competency, training effectiveness, and quality readiness for new products, processes, and teams.

 

**You have:**

* Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.
* Minimum of 10 years of proven leadership experience in the aviation or aerospace sector, with senior quality assurance experience preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of aviation maintenance and its regulatory requirements (FAA, EASA, and OEM requirements). Hands-on aviation maintenance experience may offset formal credentials.
* Experience managing quality escapes, investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action programs.
* Experience owning or managing a QMS in a regulated environment, with working knowledge of ISO 9001 (AS9100 familiarity a plus).
* Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn quality data into executive-level metrics, insights, and recommendations.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships with OEMs, customers, and leaders at all levels of the organization.
* Strategic thinking with a strong focus on results and the ability to manage complex projects and initiatives.
* Ability to lead across a multi-site, multi-region team; willingness to travel to CAMP offices, OEM, and customer sites as needed.

**Nice to have:**

* Certified ISO 9001 Internal/External Auditor (or equivalent lead auditor certification) with hands-on audit experience.
* Six Sigma Black Belt, with demonstrated process improvement results.
* Quality manager certification (e.g., ASQ CQM) or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) is a bonus.
* Experience working with large OEM contracts and high-profile customers or large fleet operators.
* Experience in aircraft maintenance tracking, engine trend monitoring, or other SaaS/data-driven service environments.

 

**Why Work at CAMP?**

Join a culture where your ideas matter, your impact is real, and your growth is supported. Be part of a team reimagining the future of aviation.

CAMP is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer – vets/disabled

CAMP is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, please contact hr@campsystems.com (mailto:hr@campsystems.com).

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status EEO.

Equal Opportunity Employer 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.
