existing_roles.title: Director of Operations
existing_roles.description:
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day operations at Innova's M3 facility in Mexicali, Mexico, including production, maintenance, purchasing, shipping and receiving, and site safety. Working closely with the site leadership team, this role ensures production goals, quality standards, cost targets, and customer delivery commitments are met. The Director builds and develops a strong local team, drives continuous improvement, and serves as the key link between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Finance, Quality, and Sales teams. The ideal candidate is based in the San Diego area, is fully bilingual in English and Spanish, and has proven experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Champion and uphold the company's values, mission, and quality policy in all activities.

* Adhere to and help enforce company policies, procedures, and internal control standards.

* Ensure compliance with all applicable Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Follow all safety rules and PPE requirements, and promptly report hazards, incidents, and near-misses.

* Lead all operations at the M3 facility, including production, maintenance, purchasing, and shipping and receiving, to meet production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery commitments.

* Direct and develop the site leadership team, including hiring, training, performance management, and succession planning.

* Oversee production planning and scheduling to balance capacity, labor, and materials with customer demand.

* Establish operational KPIs and monitor productivity, efficiency, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery, taking corrective action as needed.

* Oversee the site safety program and ensure compliance with applicable Mexican health, safety, and environmental regulations (e.g., STPS and NOM standards), fostering a strong culture of safety.

* Develop and manage the site operating budget, labor plan, and capital expenditure requests.

* Oversee equipment maintenance and facility upkeep to maximize uptime and maintain a safe, organized plant.

* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, improve throughput, and lower costs.

* Coordinate with logistics and customs partners to support cross-border shipments, materials flow, and import/export requirements.

* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, employee relations, and compliance with Mexican labor law.

* Serve as the primary liaison between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Quality, Finance, and Sales, providing regular operational and financial reporting.

* Perform other related duties as required.

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, required.

* Experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico (maquiladora or similar cross-border environment) strongly preferred.

* Experience with plastics manufacturing processes (e.g., injection molding, thermoforming, CNC machining) preferred.

* Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma certification preferred.

**SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (written and verbal) required.

* Proven leadership skills, with the ability to build, motivate, and develop a high-performing team.

* Extensive knowledge of manufacturing operations, production planning, and plant management.

* Strong working knowledge of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.

* Financial acumen, with the ability to develop budgets, manage costs, and interpret financial data.

* Working knowledge of Mexican labor, safety, and environmental regulations.

* Working knowledge of quality system requirements under ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ERP/MRP systems.

* Valid passport and ability to cross the U.S.–Mexico border regularly.

**TRAINING & COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS**

* Complete new-hire orientation and role-specific on-the-job training prior to performing unsupervised work.

* Complete Quality Management System (QMS) training applicable to this role, including quality policy awareness and the consequences of nonconformance to product or process requirements.

* Complete safety training applicable to this role (e.g., PPE use, lockout/tagout, forklift certification).

* Maintain competency through periodic refresher or retraining as required by department procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Office setting.

* Manufacturing floor environment.

* Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

* Mobility to navigate the production floor to conduct inspections and oversight.

**EXPECTED HOURS OF WORK**

* This is a full-time exempt position, required to work Monday through Friday. Occasional weekend availability may be required based on business needs.

**TRAVEL**

* Regular cross-border travel between San Diego, CA and the M3 facility in Mexicali, with on-site presence required a minimum of 4 days per week.

* Occasional travel to other Innova facilities, customers, and suppliers, up to 10%.

Pay: $110,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

existing_roles.description:
**DEFINITION:**

Under general direction from the General Manager, plans, directs, organizes, integrates and provides oversight of ReGen Monterey’s Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), equipment maintenance, site and facilities maintenance, landfill operations; scales operations, landfill gas operations, and Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) operations; directs and manages the development of short and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the Strategic Plan and annual business plan and ensures their effective execution; ensures all assigned operations and functions serve the needs of ReGen Monterey, while complying with applicable laws and regulations; responsible for maximizing the environmental management of resources; provides highly responsible and complex operations support to the General Manager.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

This position is responsible for coordination, integration and short and long-range planning of a wide variety of functions related to solid waste processing, recycling and diversion programs for ReGen Monterey. Incumbents work at an advanced professional level on complex and specialized solid waste-related operations, recycling activities, facilities, programs, and services, which include formulation and implementation of programs and financial budgets. Within assigned areas of accountability, the incumbent operates with substantial latitude and discretion to achieve effective and efficient utilization of resources in serving ReGen Monterey’s mission. Positions at this class level serve as a member of ReGen’s leadership team and provide advice and counsel to the General Manager regarding strategic policy and problem-solving issues relating to the assigned Departments and ReGen’s overall. A person appointed to the Director of Operations classification is an “at-will” employee.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*The following duties are typical of this classification and are intended only to describe the various types of work that may be performed, the level of technical complexity of the assignment(s) and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties. The omission of a specific duty statement does not exclude it from the position if the work is consistent with the concept of the classification or is similar or closely related to another duty statement to address business needs and changing business practices.*

* Oversee and is responsible for planning and execution of all aspects of solid waste and recycling operations including processing, recycling/diversion, scheduling, expansion and renovation of processing facility, and customer service.
* Oversee logistics, material preparation and export compliance of collected materials and manage all aspects of commodity sales and related contracted services.
* Oversees and is responsible for the planning and execution of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of ReGen Monterey’s landfill; oversees proper compliance with specifications on the use and development of disposal site, ensures proper operations compliance with health and safety regulations.
* Participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities of ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Plans, organizes, controls, integrates and evaluates the work of assigned departments to ensure services comply with the policies and strategic direction set by the General Manager, Board of Directors and all applicable laws and regulations.
* Recommend and enforce State waste reduction/recycling regulations and other policy issues, including safety policy and procedures.
* Manages the development, revision, and implementation of policies and procedures for ReGen Monterey’s solid waste and recycling/diversion operations.
* Drafts budget for assigned departments.
* Reviews and assesses all program production data; measures program effectiveness; prepares quarterly and annual data reports.
* Assists in the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for equipment and services; represents the division in negotiations with vendors and service contractors and participates in contract administration in disputed contractual matters.
* Prepares staff reports and letters, including reports for presentation to Board of Directors.
* All ReGen Monterey positions require the employee to provide good customer service to both internal and external customers, maintain positive and effective working relationships with other ReGen Monterey employees, and have regular and reliable attendance and timeliness. Must show cooperation and respect to fellow employees and supervisors at all times.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:**

The incumbent in this position provides direct supervision of the operations department managers and has oversight of multiple departments and indirect supervision of approximately 100 assigned department employees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Through subordinates, supervises the safe and efficient handling and disposal of solid waste, including household, industrial, infectious, medical, and household hazardous materials; provides oversight ancillary solid waste operations, including equipment maintenance and repair, recycling, and enforcement of refuse disposal laws.
* Coordinates solid waste processing operations with engineering staff to ensure the success of new programs and facilities; analyzes field operations and formulates improvements to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations; performs long-range planning for staffing needs, equipment replacement, and other operational requirements.
* Provides oversight to HHW program and organics recycling program, including food waste collection, yard waste processing, mulch/compost marketing and other waste reduction processing such as scrap metal, electronic waste, mattresses, and scrap tires.

* Prepares tonnage reports and makes recommendations regarding change in fees.
* Organize and optimize the structure of the assigned departments, adjusting in accordance with workloads and new/changing functions.
* Maintain contact with various governmental and regulatory agencies, industry related agencies, and represent ReGen Monterey at public and professional organizations functions.
* Selects and trains operations staff; assists management staff in resolving the most difficult operational problems; establishes productive standards and measures staff performance; accordingly, prepares annual performance plans, evaluates performance, and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinate managers. Collaborates with human resources with disciplinary actions.
* Directly or through subordinates, responds to complaints from ReGen Monterey customers by explaining and enforcing applicable laws and regulations; participates in public workshops to explain and generate support for proposed projects and facilities; may address the Board of Directors to answer questions about issues or proposals related to ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Oversees and participates in the annual review and revision of ReGen Monterey’s fee structure; develops strategies and approaches for evaluating fee change alternatives; directs the development and recommends proposed fees; attends and participates in public meetings; oversees the implementation of new fees following board approval.
* Directs and coordinates the preparation of analyses and recommendations regarding policy issues and long-range plans to address ReGen Monterey’s financial needs; advises the General Manager regarding policy issues, programs and projects to meet ReGen Monterey and customer needs; advises and assists the General Manager in identifying, articulating and implementing policies, programs and projects.
* Participates in the analysis of proposed legislation and regulation; participates in industry and intergovernmental activities to influence legislative and regulatory change consistent with ReGen Monterey’s interests and needs; represents ReGen Monterey as requested or assigned in dealings with stakeholders in ReGen Monterey’s service area, and with other industry and governmental agencies and professional organizations.
* Participates in major negotiations with contractors, consultants, vendors, collective bargaining and other public agencies.
* Participates in regional, state, national and other professional meetings and conferences to stay abreast of trends and technology related to ReGen Monterey’s operations, particularly in areas of assigned accountability.

**Knowledge of and Ability to:**

The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to successfully perform the assigned duties.

**Knowledge of:**

Principles and practices of recycling and diversion program operations, solid waste management and landfill maintenance practices and procedures; local, state and federal regulations pertaining to environmental management of landfills and public works systems or landfill operations; California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); principles and practices of budgeting, effective management, supervision, evaluation and training; health and safety regulations. Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint) is required.

**Ability to:**

Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals; understand highly regulatory issues (current and proposed) and appropriate permitting for solid waste facilities, recycling operations and programs; negotiate with the best interest of ReGen Monterey; work independently with minimal supervision; manage and evaluate the work of others; prepare clear and concise plans, specifications, and technical reports; interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local policies, laws, and regulations; present proposals and recommendations clearly, logically and persuasively in public meetings; develop and implement appropriate procedures and controls; exercise sound, independent judgment within policy guidelines; develop and administer departmental goals, objectives, and procedures; analyze and assess programs, policies, and operational needs and make appropriate adjustments; research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods and techniques; facilitate group participation and consensus building; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

**TRAINING, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental planning and management; environmental studies; solid waste planning or a related field is required.

**Experience:**

* Ten to 15 years of broad and progressively responsible work experience in recycling program operations, transfer station management, or combined and related experiences.
* A minimum of five years of recent experience in solid waste management and/or in the operation of mixed waste processing facility or a single-stream material recovery facility or operation of a landfill is required. **OR** work experience in a management position with a private or public agency responsible for solid waste management, recycling/diversion or landfill operations to demonstrate knowledge, skills, and abilities to meet the above minimum requirements.

**License or Certificate:**

* Possession of or ability to obtain a certificate of Manager of Landfill Operations (MOLO) issued by the Solid Waste Association of North America (SWANA) is desired.
* Possession of a valid California driver’s license is required.

**PhYSICAL AND SENSORY REQUIREMENTS:**

The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by employees to successfully perform the essential functions of this class. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Physical Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to sit; talk or hear, in person, in meetings and by telephone; use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; and reach with hands and arms; occasionally bend, stoop, lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 25 pounds individually. Employees are occasionally required to walk and stand on even and uneven surfaces, grounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

**Mental Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to use written and oral communication skills; read and interpret complex data, information and documents; analyze and solve complex policy and operational problems; observe and interpret people and situations; use math and mathematical reasoning; learn and apply new information or skills; perform highly detailed work on multiple, concurrent tasks with constant interruptions; work under intensive deadlines and interact with Board members, all levels of ReGen Monterey management, other elected and appointed governmental officials, consultants, contractors, developers, vendors, employees, media representatives and the public.

**Special Demands**

Must be able to actively participate in public meetings, including giving presentations in person and on camera before the Board of Directors and members of the public.

**Work Environment**

Employees work under typical office conditions, and the noise level is usually quiet, occasional exposure to dirt, grease, foul odors and other outdoor elements.

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager
existing_roles.description:
**Compensation Range:**

$122,800 - $204,600

**Plant Manager**

Department: Operations / Manufacturing

Reports To: Director of Operations

Direct Reports: Production Managers, Facilities Manager, and other assigned manufacturing leadership

Scope: Three manufacturing buildings / multi-product HVAC manufacturing operation

**Position**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and day-to-day execution of manufacturing operations across three buildings within a large HVAC manufacturing facility. This position provides hands-on leadership to ensure the plant safely produces high-quality products on schedule, at the required volume and cost, while developing a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating production activities across multiple manufacturing processes and buildings, including assembly, sheet metal fabrication, welding, piping/refrigeration, testing, material flow, and final product completion.

The successful candidate will establish clear operating standards, drive cross-functional accountability, develop manufacturing leadership, remove operational constraints, and ensure the plant has the people, processes, equipment, and infrastructure required to support current production and future growth.

This position is expected to be highly visible on the manufacturing floor and serves as the primary operational leader responsible for translating business objectives into daily execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Plant Leadership & Operational Execution**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for manufacturing operations across all three buildings.
* Establish daily, weekly, and monthly operating priorities aligned with business requirements.
* Ensure production plans are executed safely, efficiently, and according to customer commitments.
* Maintain strong communication and coordination between buildings and manufacturing departments.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability for production performance.
* Lead daily plant operating reviews and ensure corrective actions are completed.
* Identify and remove constraints affecting throughput, capacity, quality, or delivery.
* Maintain appropriate production capacity, staffing, equipment, and infrastructure to support business growth.
* Ensure standardized processes are consistently followed across all buildings.
* Maintain a strong management presence on the manufacturing floor.

**2. Production Management**

* Lead Production Managers and ensure effective management of production personnel.
* Establish production priorities based on customer demand, capacity, material availability, and schedule requirements.
* Ensure production schedules are achieved while balancing labor, equipment, materials, and testing capacity.
* Monitor production flow from fabrication through final assembly and testing.
* Develop and maintain effective production metrics and visual management systems.
* Identify bottlenecks and implement corrective actions to improve throughput.
* Ensure appropriate escalation processes are in place when production performance is at risk.
* Coordinate production activities between the three buildings to maximize overall plant capacity.

**3. Safety, Environmental & Compliance**

* Establish safety as the facility’s highest operational priority.
* Partner with EHS leadership to maintain a strong safety culture across all three buildings.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, company requirements, and applicable industry standards.
* Drive accountability for safe work practices at all levels of the organization.
* Ensure timely investigation and corrective action following incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
* Support programs designed to reduce injuries, ergonomic risks, environmental impacts, and workplace hazards.
* Ensure employees receive appropriate safety training and understand their responsibilities.

**4. Quality**

* Partner with Quality leadership to ensure products meet customer, engineering, and company requirements.
* Establish accountability for first-time quality and defect prevention.
* Drive reduction of scrap, rework, warranty issues, and production defects.
* Ensure quality issues are rapidly escalated and contained.
* Support root-cause analysis and corrective-action processes.
* Promote quality at the source rather than relying on downstream inspection.
* Maintain compliance with the plant's quality management system and ISO requirements.

**5. Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead the implementation and sustainability of Lean Manufacturing Principles throughout all three buildings.
* Establish a culture of continuous improvement and employee involvement.
* Drive 5S, visual management, standardized work, problem solving, waste elimination, and flow improvements.
* Support Value Stream Mapping and improvement of end-to-end product flow.
* Establish measurable improvement targets for productivity, quality, delivery, inventory, and cost.
* Partner with Lean/Manufacturing Engineering leadership to prioritize improvement projects based on business impact.
* Ensure Lean improvements are sustained through management systems and standard work.
* Develop frontline leaders capable of independently identifying and solving operational problems.

**6. People Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Develop a high-performing manufacturing leadership team.
* Establish clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Coach and develop Production Managers, Supervisors, and other manufacturing leaders.
* Identify organizational capability gaps and work with Human Resources to develop staffing and development plans.
* Support workforce planning and hiring activities necessary to meet production requirements.
* Establish effective onboarding and training processes for new employees.
* Develop succession plans for key manufacturing positions.
* Promote employee engagement, teamwork, ownership, and accountability.
* Address performance issues promptly and consistently.

**7. Capacity & Business Growth**

* Develop manufacturing capacity plans to support current and future customer demand.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Finance, Materials, and other functions to identify capacity requirements.
* Evaluate labor, equipment, floor space, testing, utilities, and infrastructure requirements.
* Support capital planning and justification for new equipment and facility improvements.
* Ensure new production areas and buildings are effectively integrated into the overall manufacturing system.
* Develop ramp-up plans for new products, programs, and production transfers.
* Ensure the plant can scale production without compromising safety, quality, or delivery performance.

**8. Cross-Functional Leadership**

Work closely with:

* Director of Operations
* Production
* Materials
* Production Planning
* Logistics
* Quality
* EHS
* Lean / Manufacturing Engineering
* Facilities
* Maintenance
* Engineering
* Finance
* Human Resources
* Supply Chain
* Sales / Customer teams

Ensure cross-functional issues are identified early, assigned to the appropriate owner, and driven to resolution.

**9. Facilities, Equipment & Infrastructure**

* Partner with Facilities and Maintenance leadership to ensure buildings, utilities, production equipment, cranes, test infrastructure, and other critical assets support production requirements.
* Establish preventive and predictive maintenance expectations.
* Ensure critical production equipment has appropriate contingency plans.
* Support capital equipment selection, installation, commissioning, and production launch.
* Ensure facility expansion projects are integrated into manufacturing operations with minimal disruption to production.

**10. Performance Management & Accountability**

Establish and maintain a plant operating system based on measurable performance.

Key performance indicators should include:

Safety

* Recordable incident rate
* Lost-time incidents
* Near misses
* Safety observations
* Corrective-action closure

Quality

* First-pass yield
* Scrap
* Rework
* Customer defects
* Warranty / quality escapes

Delivery

* On-time delivery
* Schedule attainment
* Production attainment
* Manufacturing lead time
* Test-bay utilization / throughput

Productivity

* Labor productivity
* Units per labor hour
* OEE where applicable
* Direct labor efficiency
* Throughput

Cost

* Manufacturing cost
* Labor variance
* Scrap cost
* Overtime
* Cost of poor quality

Lean

* 5S performance
* Kaizen completion
* Standard work compliance
* Improvement savings
* Value-stream performance

The Plant Manager will ensure performance is reviewed routinely and that corrective actions have clearly identified owners and due dates.

**Leadership Expectations**

The Plant Manager is expected to:

* Lead from the floor rather than from the office.
* Establish a culture of accountability without creating a culture of blame.
* Make decisions based on facts and data.
* Escalate issues early rather than allowing problems to become emergencies.
* Develop leaders instead of personally solving every problem.
* Maintain a strong focus on safety and quality while driving production.
* Create alignment between the three buildings rather than allowing them to operate as independent plants.
* Establish consistent standards and expectations across the operation.
* Communicate clearly with employees, leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Demonstrate urgency while maintaining disciplined problem solving.
* Build an organization capable of supporting significant business growth.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field preferred.
* 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 3+ years of plant or multi-department manufacturing management experience.
* Experience managing large manufacturing organizations, multiple production areas, and facilities.
* Experience in HVAC, refrigeration, industrial equipment, sheet metal, welding, assembly, or related manufacturing strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing significant production growth or plant expansion.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience managing safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance.
* Strong financial and business acumen.
* Experience developing and leading supervisors and managers.
* Strong communication and organizational skills.
* Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth manufacturing environment.

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager
existing_roles.description:
Description:

The Plant Manager is a senior leader responsible for planning, directing, and controlling activities of a plant to accomplish budgeted operational and financial objectives. Directs all functions at the plant including production, quality control, finance, purchasing, inventory control, manufacturing, engineering, and employee relations. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, data-driven leader capable of scaling production capacity, optimizing labor efficiency, managing complex capital projects, and building a high-performing, engaged workforce.

This role is responsible for the achievement of all operational financial goals. The responsibility also includes establishing and managing operational policies and procedures, creating and maintaining a safe and quality-minded work environment, and fostering the development of a well-trained and motivated work force at all levels.

LALA US Omaha Dairy manufactures yogurt smoothies and pourable sour cream. The facility provides a clean work environment, well-lit, highly automated production facility and career advancement opportunities. LALA US provides a competitive total compensation package including:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401k with company match
* Vacation and Personal time off
* 10 paid holidays
* Company-paid life, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability insurance
* Employee Assistance Program

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. People leadership, talent development & labor relations**

* Recruit, mentor, and evaluate department manager, superintendent and shift supervisors, establishing clear accountability and succession plans.
* Foster positive employee relations, high retention, and strong shop-floor morale through transparent communication, town halls, and recognition programs.
* Manage collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and constructive relationships with union leadership.

**2. Production & operational execution**

* Direct multi-shift manufacturing operations to consistently achieve daily, weekly, and monthly production schedules and On-Time In-Full delivery targets.
* Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including Overall Equipment Effectiveness, scrap rates, yield, labor variance, and cycle times.
* Optimize production scheduling, capacity planning, and bottleneck management in partnership with Supply Chain and Materials teams.

**3. Financial management & P&L ownership**

* Develop, manage, and justify the annual plant operating budget, focusing on direct/indirect labor costs, raw material utilization, and overhead absorption.
* Track, analyze, and drive corrective actions on manufacturing cost variances, specifically Material Usage Variance, Labor Efficiency Variance, Scrap/Yield losses to protect margins.
* Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain to investigate unfavorable material usage variances caused by Bill of Materials inaccuracies, machine calibration drift, or substandard raw materials.
* Conduct monthly financial variance reviews with corporate finance to identify cost-saving opportunities and mitigate inflationary pressures.

**4. Continuous improvement & operational excellence**

* Embed Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies (CILA, Centerline, 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, TPM, SMED) into daily floor operations.
* Lead cross-functional continuous improvement events aimed at eliminating waste, reducing changeover times, and improving throughput.
* Leverage Manufacturing Execution Systems and ERP data to drive predictive decision-making and real-time floor visibility.

**5. Environmental, health, and safety leadership**

* Champion a zero-incident safety culture by enforcing strict adherence to OSHA regulations, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures, and company safety policies.
* Lead root-cause investigations for all near-misses, recordable incidents, and environmental excursions, ensuring timely corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
* Oversee environmental compliance, including EPA permitting, hazardous waste disposal, emissions monitoring, and sustainability targets.

**6. Quality assurance & regulatory compliance**

* Partner with the Quality Manager to reduce Customer Complaints, Cost of Poor Quality, and internal rework.
* Ensure the facility maintains strict compliance with industry quality standards (GMP, & SQF).
* Lead internal, customer, and third-party regulatory audits with zero major non-conformances.

**7. Maintenance, reliability & facilities management**

* Partner with the Engineering manager to achieve the goals on the Preventive and Predictive Maintenance programs to maximize asset reliability and minimize unplanned downtime.
* Ensure spare parts inventory management is optimized to balance carrying costs with equipment uptime requirements.
* Maintain physical plant infrastructure, utilities, security, and building compliance.

**Core Competencies & Attitudes**

* **Unbeatable attitude & resilience**: Maintains an optimistic, "can-do" mindset in the face of complex operational challenges, viewing equipment breakdowns, supply chain disruptions, and cost variances as solvable problems rather than roadblocks.
* **Passion for manufacturing excellence:** Brings genuine energy, pride, and enthusiasm to the shop floor, inspiring teams to take ownership of their craft and strive for world-class production standards.
* **Relentless focus on results:** Operates with a strong bias for execution and goal attainment, consistently driving teams to hit SQCDME targets and protect plant profitability.
* **Hands-on mindset:** Leads from the shop floor rather than behind a desk; actively walks the floor to observe processes, engage with operators, and solve problems at the source.
* **Extreme ownership & accountability:** Takes full responsibility for plant outcomes to engage the team can be focused on results.
* **Data-driven curiosity:** Approaches operational bottlenecks and cost variances (like Material Usage Variance) with analytical rigor, relying on root-cause data rather than guesswork.
* **Action & sense of urgency:** Responds swiftly to equipment downtime, safety hazards, and quality escapes while keeping teams calm and focused under pressure.
* **Servant leadership & empathy:** Listens actively to frontline workers, removes roadblocks for supervisors, and treats every team member with fairness and respect.
* **Continuous growth & adaptability:** Embraces change, challenges "*the way we've always done it"* and encourages calculated experimentation to improve efficiency.

**Core Soft Skills**

* **Multi-level communication:** Ability to translate complex operational metrics into strategic business updates for corporate executives, while communicating daily goals clearly and respectfully to frontline operators.
* **Conflict resolution & de-escalation:** Skilled at mediating disputes between competing departments and resolving shop-floor personnel conflicts calmly and fairly.
* **Emotional Intelligence:** Reads the moral and stress levels of the workforce, maintaining composure during crises like major line breakdowns, customer audits, or supply chain disruptions.
* **Cross-functional Influence:** Builds strong partnerships without direct authority over supporting teams to secure resources and align priorities.
* **Coaching & talent multiplication:** Focuses on developing future leaders by delegating effectively, giving constructive feedback, and empowering supervisors to make independent decisions rather than micromanaging.
* **Active listening:** Creates psychological safety on the plant floor so operators feel comfortable reporting near-misses, quality issues, or process inefficiencies early.
* **Stakeholder & customer relationship:** Represents the facility professionally during high-stakes customer visits, supplier negotiations, and community or regulatory inspections.

Requirements:

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Chemical), Operations Management, Supply Chain, or Business Administration.
* **Experience:** 10+ years of progressive manufacturing experience, with at least 5 years in a Plant Manager, Assistant Plant Manager, or Operations Manager role overseeing 100+ employees.
* **Financial expertise:** Demonstrated experience managing a multi-million-dollar plant P&L, standard costing. Demonstrate understanding of managing budgets and controlling costs.
* **Systems proficiency:** Advanced working knowledge of SAP, MES platforms, and demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
* **Methodology expertise:** Proven track record of implementing Lean tools and driving measurable improvements in OEE, scrap reduction, and productivity. Working knowledge of Six Sigma, LEAN and/or Continuous Improvement principles, especially as they apply to a manufacturing environment

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration or master’s in engineering management.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification.
* Desirable food/beverage manufacturing plant operations experience, dairy experience strongly preferred

**Work Environment & Physical Demands**

* Split between an office environment and an active manufacturing floor with exposure to moving mechanical parts, varying noise levels, and temperature fluctuations.
* Requires regular walking/standing on the production floor and occasional travel (<5%) to corporate headquarters, conferences, suppliers, or sister facilities.

LALA US is an equal opportunity employer. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an at-will relationship.

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager
existing_roles.description:
CAMS is looking for a Plant Manager at the Kings Mountain Energy Center in Kings Mountain, NC. The incumbent will have 19 direct and indirect employees. The Plant Manager is responsible for the safe, reliable, compliant, and financially responsible operation and maintenance of the Kings Mountain Energy Center.

Kings Mountain Energy Center is a 475MW natural gas-fired combined-cycle power plant. The facility features an advanced 276MW Mitsubishi M501GAC gas turbine, a Vogt Power heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), a 225MW Toshiba steam turbine generator, and a Thermal Engineering International surface condenser.

The position provides overall leadership for plant operations, maintenance, engineering support, environmental and regulatory compliance, administration, workforce development, budgeting, outage execution, and continuous improvement. The Plant Manager serves as the primary site representative to CAMS leadership, facility ownership and asset management, and is accountable for developing a high-performing organization that maximizes plant availability, reliability, efficiency, and long-term asset value. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong leadership, sound technical and business judgment, and the ability to manage a complex combined-cycle generating facility in a competitive power-market environment.

### **Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for the safe, reliable, environmentally compliant, and cost-effective operation and maintenance of the facility.
* Establish and maintain a strong safety culture in which employees and contractors actively identify hazards, stop unsafe work, and demonstrate personal ownership of safety performance.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental permits, laws, regulations, NERC requirements, OSHA requirements, company policies, and facility procedures.
* Lead and develop the plant management team and workforce, including recruiting, coaching, performance management, succession planning, qualification programs, and workforce development.
* Maintain effective working relationships with facility ownership, Asset Management, CAMS leadership, regulatory agencies, the system operator, utilities, OEMs, contractors, and other key stakeholders.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, O&M budgets, capital plans, forecasts, and long-term maintenance strategies consistent with owner objectives and contractual requirements.
* Monitor plant financial performance and control expenditures while ensuring that short-term budget objectives do not create unacceptable safety, environmental, reliability, or long-term asset risk.
* Direct plant operations to achieve availability, reliability, heat-rate, start-reliability, capacity, and other performance objectives while meeting dispatch and commercial obligations.
* Provide leadership for maintenance strategies, preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective-maintenance backlog management, equipment reliability, root-cause analysis, and elimination of recurring failures.
* Direct planning and execution of combustion turbine, steam turbine, HRSG, generator, electrical, and balance-of-plant outages and major maintenance activities, including scope, budget, schedule, contractor performance, quality, and risk management.
* Develop and maintain multi-year outage, major-maintenance, and capital improvement plans based on equipment condition, OEM recommendations, operating profile, commercial requirements, and risk.
* Identify significant plant risks and provide CAMS leadership and ownership with timely information, alternatives, consequences, and clear recommendations for decision-making.
* Ensure appropriate critical-spares strategy, inventory controls, long-lead component planning, and equipment-obsolescence management.
* Oversee plant engineering and technical support activities, including equipment modifications, controls and logic changes, performance monitoring, capital projects, and technical problem solving.
* Ensure plant procedures, drawings, technical documentation, training materials, emergency plans, and operating records are accurate and maintained.
* Oversee administration of applicable plant contracts and agreements and ensure operational compliance with owner requirements, O&M obligations, OEM/LTSA requirements, fuel and utility agreements, and other commercial commitments.
* Maintain effective communication with Asset Management and ownership, including prompt escalation of significant safety, environmental, operational, equipment, financial, contractual, or regulatory events.
* Lead emergency response and business-continuity activities and ensure the facility is prepared for severe weather, grid emergencies, fuel interruptions, cyber events, and major equipment failures.
* Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, continuous improvement, and open communication across Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Compliance, and Administration.
* Identify and implement opportunities to improve plant performance, reduce operating risk, optimize costs, and increase long-term asset value.
* Support CAMS fleet initiatives, peer reviews, lessons learned, workforce-development efforts, and cross-facility technical support as requested.

Other duties as assigned.

### **Qualifications and Skills**

* 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in power generation operations and maintenance, including significant leadership experience in a power plant environment.
* Prior Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Maintenance Manager, or comparable senior power-generation leadership experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge of combined-cycle power plant operations, maintenance, reliability, and major equipment systems. Experience with combustion turbines, steam turbines, HRSGs, generators, electrical systems, and balance-of-plant equipment is preferred.
* Experience with Mitsubishi M501GAC combustion turbines is preferred.
* Demonstrated experience planning and executing major outages, managing contractors and OEMs, controlling outage scope and cost, and resolving emergent technical issues.
* Working knowledge of environmental, health and safety, and electric-generation regulatory requirements applicable to power plant operations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and managing O&M budgets, forecasts, capital projects, and long-term maintenance plans.
* Proven ability to lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable a multidisciplinary workforce.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, planning, and organizational skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with employees, executives, owners, regulators, contractors, and technical personnel.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred. Significant relevant power-generation leadership experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems, plant historians, performance-monitoring systems, and other power-plant business systems.
* Ability to respond to plant emergencies and significant operating events outside normal business hours as required.

Other Desirable Skills

* Demonstrates visible leadership and a strong personal commitment to safety and environmental compliance.
* Balances technical, operational, financial, and commercial considerations when making decisions.
* Communicates significant risks and problems early and avoids surprises for ownership and senior leadership.
* Demonstrates strong customer service skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with facility ownership and Asset Management.
* Effectively prioritizes competing demands in a fast-changing operating environment.
* Develop people and create clear succession paths for key positions.
* Demonstrates a high degree of integrity, accountability, sound judgment, and ownership mentality.
* Ability to represent the facility and CAMS professionally with owners, regulators, industry organizations, and external stakeholders

Applicants must possess a **valid driver's license** and maintain a clean driving record, as this position requires occasional travel for company business. Candidates should be comfortable operating a vehicle as part of their job responsibilities and must meet any applicable company and insurance requirements.

CAMS offers a variety of excellent benefits. Full-time employees are offered the following: medical, dental, vision, LTD, STD, and Life insurance plans. You can even select additional “al la carte” benefits to meet all your needs. You can also enroll in our 401k, flex spending accounts for medical and childcare needs, and participate in our employee referral and tuition reimbursement programs.

Qualified Applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States. Qualified Applicants will not require employer sponsored work authorization now or in the future for employment in the United States.

We believe in transparency and providing candidates with important information to make informed decisions. The salary range for this position will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, and location. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to skills, experience, and relevant qualifications.

This range represents the base salary and does not include other forms of compensation, such as bonuses, benefits, or equity, which may be offered in addition to the base pay. The company reserves the right to modify.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

**Position Summary**

Location: South San Francisco, CA

Neurona Therapeutics is a clinical stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco focused on the development of neuronal cell-based therapies for intractable neurological diseases.  
We are seeking a Senior Manager, External Manufacturing who will lead our relationships with CMOs/CDMOs and critical suppliers supporting the company’s cell therapy pipeline. This role owns external manufacturing partnerships end to end, from partner selection, onboarding, and technology transfer through campaign execution and ongoing performance management, to ensure reliable, high-quality, and cost-effective manufacturing. The role also supports clinical supply needs by aligning external manufacturing output with clinical program timelines.

The role will partner closely with Technical Operations, Quality, CMC, Procurement, Clinical Operations, and senior leadership to drive strategic partner decisions, resolve risks, and build a scalable external manufacturing network. This is a high-visibility opportunity to shape the external manufacturing strategy of an innovative, growing cell therapy company.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Serve as the primary relationship owner for CMOs/CDMOs and critical suppliers, leading governance forums, joint steering committees, and executive-level engagement.
* Lead partner selection, due diligence, contracting support, and onboarding, including quality and supply agreements in partnership with Quality, Legal, and Procurement.
* Oversee technology transfers, process readiness, and manufacturing campaigns at external partners, driving timelines, deliverables, and issue resolution.
* Define and track partner performance metrics (delivery, quality, capacity, cost, and responsiveness); lead business reviews and improvement plans.
* Manage external manufacturing schedules, capacity planning, and batch-record and deliverable timelines across partners.
* Partner with Quality and Technical Operations on supplier qualification, audits, changes, deviations, CAPAs, and other GMP-related activities.
* Lead negotiation and management of commercial terms, pricing, change orders, and budgets in collaboration with Procurement and Finance.
* Proactively mitigate risks to partner capacity, critical materials, lead times, and supplier continuity; lead contingency and alternate-source strategies.
* Report on partner performance, risks, and mitigation plans to cross-functional stakeholders and senior leadership; mentor team members as the organization grows.
* Align external manufacturing output with clinical program timelines, working with the clinical supply team on forecasting, inventory planning, and IRT/RTSM needs.
* Support oversight of GMP packaging and manufacturing activities for clinical supply at external partners.
* Travel: Approximately 20–30% to CMO/CDMO and supplier sites, with flexibility based on program needs

**Qualifications**  
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Life Sciences, Engineering, Business, or related field; advanced degree a plus.

* Strong understanding of GMP requirements and biotech/pharmaceutical manufacturing and supply-chain processes.
* Strong leadership, relationship-management, negotiation, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and external partners.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, clinical-stage environment.

**Preferred**

* Cell therapy or advanced therapy experience.
* Experience with supplier qualification, quality agreements, contract negotiations, and change order and budget management.
* Clinical supply chain experience, including forecasting, inventory planning, IRT/RTSM, and GMP packaging oversight.
* Experience in both small biotech (self-driven, requiring problem solving and flexibility) and larger biopharma (more structured training and processes).

existing_roles.title: Director, Strategy & Operations
existing_roles.description:
**The Problem**

Severe mental illness affects over 15 million adults in the United States. Schizophrenia. Schizoaffective disorder. Bipolar I. Treatment-resistant depression. These are the conditions the rest of healthcare has systematically failed to build for.

What makes this problem different from most of healthcare is that the tools to solve it do not exist. The clinical protocols, the measurement science, the precision medicine, the technology to deliver coordinated longitudinal outpatient care for this population. None of it has been built. This is a frontier problem, and it requires frontier science and care delivery to solve.

We are developing all of it. The care, the science, the technology.

**Who We Are**

Amae Health is a Series B, venture-backed Public Benefit Corporation delivering specialty outpatient care for people with severe mental illness through high-acuity, in-person clinics nationwide.

Our integrated model brings psychiatry, therapy, primary care, dietitians, and community support together under one roof. Leading health systems—including **New York-Presbyterian, Cedars-Sinai, Mass General Brigham, Novant Health, and CommonSpirit**—collaborate with us to expand this level of care.

Alongside care delivery, we are building the science and technology the field has long lacked—proprietary clinical protocols, novel measurement, and an AI-driven data platform designed for severe mental illness.

The impact: fewer hospitalizations, greater stability, and more people living meaningful lives in their communities.

**The Team**

We are clinicians, operators, technologists, and scientists who chose Amae because the problem is hard and the stakes are real. We are not interested in incremental improvements to a broken system—we are redefining it.

Every function—finance, product, people, growth, technology—exists to serve one goal: better outcomes for the people we care for.

**The Role**

Amae Health is looking for a **Director of Strategy & Operations** to help scale a fundamentally new model of care for individuals with severe mental illness. This is a high-impact, hands-on leadership role spanning **market expansion, growth, and operational excellence**.

You'll work closely with executive, clinical, and operational leaders to **launch new markets, accelerate growth in existing ones, and build the systems that enable Amae to scale**. From developing go-to-market strategies to solving complex operational challenges, you'll turn ambitious goals into measurable results.

We're looking for a **strategic thinker who loves to execute** — someone who can see the big picture, dive into the details, and build what doesn't yet exist.

  

**What You'll Own**

* **Drive market expansion and new launches.** Lead go-to-market strategy and execution for new clinics, services, and markets — from identifying opportunities and developing launch plans to ensuring successful rollout and early performance.
* **Own high-impact growth and operational initiatives.** Identify and lead the highest-leverage opportunities to accelerate growth, improve referral conversion, strengthen care delivery, and increase operational efficiency.
* **Build the playbook for scale.** Design the operating models, processes, and performance management systems that allow Amae to grow rapidly without compromising quality or consistency of care.
* **Turn complex problems into measurable results.** Use data, frontline insights, and structured problem-solving to uncover bottlenecks, develop solutions, and drive improvements from hypothesis through implementation.
* **Lead across functions to make things happen.** Partner with clinical, operations, growth, and product leaders to translate strategic priorities into coordinated execution, navigating ambiguity and driving accountability along the way.
* **Shape how Amae operates as we grow.** Work closely with senior leadership to tackle emerging business challenges, test new approaches, and turn what works into repeatable systems across our care delivery network.

**What You'll Bring**

* **7+ years of experience** in strategy, operations, growth, or general management, ideally in a high-growth startup, consulting firm, or healthcare organization.
* **A track record of turning strategy into results.** You've owned complex, high-impact initiatives from identifying the opportunity to driving execution and delivering measurable outcomes.
* **A builder's mindset.** You thrive in ambiguity, move quickly, and are energized by creating structure, processes, and solutions where no playbook exists.
* **Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.** You can break down ambiguous problems, use data to inform decisions, and balance strategic thinking with practical execution.
* **Commercial instincts.** You're excited to drive growth, expand into new markets, build partnerships, and identify opportunities to improve business performance.
* **The ability to lead through influence.** You're collaborative, high-EQ, and effective at aligning diverse stakeholders — from frontline clinical teams to executive leadership — without relying on formal authority.
* **A genuine connection to our mission.** Healthcare experience is a plus, not a prerequisite. You're motivated by the opportunity to transform care for individuals with severe mental illness.
* **Based in the SF Bay Area**, with the ability to work in person five days a week at our Cow Hollow office.

**What We're Building**

Most healthcare companies ask you to optimize an existing system. We're building one that has never existed.

* A national care model designed for the highest-acuity patients in behavioral health.
* Precision medicine for severe mental illness, using multimodal clinical, behavioral, and social data to personalize treatment.
* A clinical operating system that integrates longitudinal data, real-time patient signals, and purpose-built tools into a single decision layer.
* New science and measurement frameworks to define what real outcomes look like in SMI—stability, functional improvement, and hospitalizations avoided.
* A health-system partnership model proving coordinated SMI care can work at scale.

If you want to maintain the status quo, this isn't the place. If you want to build what doesn't exist yet—and change how an entire population receives care—keep reading.

**What We Value**

**We center care in all we do.** Empathy is not a brand value. It's how we make clinical decisions, build products, and treat each other.

**We challenge convention.** The existing system is the problem. We question it, we test alternatives, and we move with urgency when something works.

**We take the work seriously, not ourselves.** High standards and humanity are not in tension. We hold a hard bar for quality while leaving room for humor and levity.

**Your job isn't done until the job is done.** We close gaps, we follow through, and we don't hide behind titles or org charts.

**We win together and fail together.** We own outcomes as a team. We learn fast. We don't do blame.

**We hustle with humility.** Speed matters. So does integrity. We assume best intent and stay grounded in the mission.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Amae Health is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. **Base salary range for this role is $165,000–$200,000 per year**, adjusted to market cost; the compensation package may include equity. Total compensation includes comprehensive medical/dental/vision, unlimited PTO, parental leave, and programs built around employee well-being. We'll share specifics during the interview process.

*Amae Health is building the care platform, the precision medicine, and the frontier science that severe mental illness has never had. If you want to be part of creating something this hard and this important, something that has never been done, we'd like to talk.*

We save lives while providing the opportunity for people to realize their healthy selves.:

**Director of Virtual Operations**

**Monte Nido**

**Remote**

Monte Nido has been delivering treatment for eating disorders for over three decades. Our programs offer a model of treatment that blends medically sophisticated care with a personalized treatment approach. Our work is grounded in evidence-based strategies for adults and adolescents suffering from eating disorders. We work from a multi-disciplinary treatment team approach while integrating state-of-the-art medical, psychiatric, nutritional, and clinical strategies to provide comprehensive care within an intimate home setting.

The Director of Virtual Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for Monte Nido’s virtual programs in accordance with the organization’s philosophy and mission. Reporting to the Vice President of Virtual Programs, the Director leads the Program Manager and Group Facilitation Senior Manager, establishes consistent operating standards, and ensures effective coordination across program operations, group facilitation, clinical leadership, quality, compliance, and support functions. The role is accountable for staffing and capacity planning, scheduling and coverage, attendance and census processes, documentation and clinical quality oversight, regulatory readiness, performance measurement, process improvement, and resolution of escalated operational and safety concerns. The Director translates organizational priorities into reliable execution, develops leaders, uses data to identify risks and opportunities, and advances safe, high-quality, efficient virtual care.

Schedule: Monday-Friday

Salary: $75k-$85k annually plus bonus

Total Rewards::

Discover a rewarding career with us and enjoy an array of comprehensive benefits! We prioritize your success and well-being, providing:

* Competitive compensation
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage (Benefits At a Glance)
* Retirement
* Company-paid life insurance, AD&D, and short-term disability
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* Paid time off
* Professional development
* And many more!

We are committed to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

Responsibilities Include::

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**  
1. Provide strategic and operational leadership for virtual program operations, translating organizational priorities into clear plans, standards, and measurable outcomes.  
2. Lead, coach, and supervise the Program Manager/Coordinator and Group Facilitation Senior Manager, including goal setting, performance management, career development, succession planning, and corrective action when needed.  
3. Establish operating expectations across program administration and group facilitation, ensuring leaders maintain consistent practices for staffing, scheduling, coverage, attendance, documentation, client engagement, and escalation.  
4. Maintain oversight of staffing models, schedules, capacity, and coverage across virtual programs; anticipate resource needs and escalate material risks with clear recommendations.  
5. Own program schedules across virtual services, including schedule design, maintenance, and communication; identify availability limitations and escalate constraints that may affect access, coverage, or continuity of care to Clinical Directors and other appropriate clinical leaders.  
6. Oversee attendance, census, engagement, discharge, outcomes, client satisfaction, and operational performance indicators; use trends to improve retention, quality, and efficiency.  
7. Ensure reliable documentation and clinical quality audit processes, including timely corrective follow-up, retraining, chart completion, required signatures, and maintenance of program records.  
8. Direct operational readiness for Joint Commission, payer, licensing, and internal audits in partnership with clinical, quality, compliance, billing, and human resources leaders.  
9. Ensure virtual-program policies, procedures, care schedules, handbooks, workflows, and telehealth standards remain current, practical, and consistently implemented.  
10. Partner with clinical and medical leaders to resolve escalated client safety, attendance, staffing, documentation, and program-quality concerns while preserving appropriate clinical decision-making authority.  
11. Partner with Clinical Directors to develop and implement quality-of-care initiatives, monitor effectiveness, address identified gaps, and support consistent standards across virtual programs.  
12. Define performance expectations for operational functions and hold leaders accountable for employee development, engagement, conduct, productivity, and consistent application of policies in partnership with Human Resources.  
13. Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve workflows, technology use, communication, service quality, and the experience of clients, families, employees, and referral partners.  
14. Communicate significant operational, safety, quality, compliance, and resource risks to the Vice President of Virtual Programs with timely analysis and recommended actions.  
15. Represent virtual operations in required leadership and management meetings and facilitate decision-making, implementation, and follow-through across stakeholder groups.

**Additional Duties and Responsibilities**  
1. Support insurance, compliance, personnel-file, referral-partner, outpatient-provider, and discharge-transition activities when operational leadership is needed.  
2. Provide executive-ready updates on virtual program performance, risks, priorities, and improvement initiatives.  
3. Maintain professionalism, confidentiality, sound judgment, and respectful communication in all interactions.  
4. Adhere to Monte Nido & Affiliates policies, procedures, telehealth etiquette, and safety standards, and ensure assigned leaders reinforce them consistently.  
5. Provide additional operational leadership and complete other duties as assigned.  
6. VIRTUAL EMPLOYEES: We have the same expectations for employees as we do for Cares. We ask that you keep your camera on and join from a private space free of noise and distractions (e.g., not from a car) when meeting with Cares or joining a clinical staff meeting. You will need a reliable video conferencing setup, including a camera, microphone, and stable, high-speed Internet connection. You must also be prepared with a backup plan in the event of technology failures. We expect you to consider your personal appearance in much the same way you would when seeing Cares in person. You must also keep your background clean and professional.

Qualifications::

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, behavioral health, business, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred. An equivalent combination of education and directly relevant leadership experience may be considered.
* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in behavioral health, healthcare operations, or a comparable care-delivery environment, including at least three years of people leadership. Experience leading managers, overseeing virtual operations, managing multi-program workflows, and supporting accreditation, payer, and regulatory requirements is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop managers, establish clear expectations, and drive accountability across multiple programs and functions
* Strong operational judgment, change leadership, project management, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Ability to interpret operational and quality data, identify trends, manage risk, and implement sustainable improvements.
* Knowledge of Joint Commission standards, payer requirements, patient confidentiality laws, telehealth requirements, and organizational compliance expectations.

The Opportunity
  
  
The St. Jude Leadership Academy is building the systems, experiences and capabilities that help leaders across St. Jude grow their impact. We’re looking for a Director of Academy Operations who can help turn that vision into an enterprise-scale reality.

As the Academy’s primary operational leader and integrator, you’ll translate strategy into an integrated portfolio of work and create the infrastructure needed to move ideas from concept through implementation, evaluation and scale. You’ll work across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and institutional partners to connect priorities, clarify ownership and turn complex, cross-functional work into coordinated action.

  
  

You’ll also serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership, bringing visibility to priorities, tradeoffs, resources and execution risks while helping shape how the Academy delivers its work across St. Jude.

  
  

Because the Leadership Academy operates as a small, highly collaborative team, this isn’t a role where strategy gets handed off once the plan is built. You’ll move comfortably between enterprise-level thinking and hands-on execution, building the systems that allow a small team to have an outsized impact across St. Jude.

  
  

### **What You’ll Do**

  
  

As Director of Academy Operations, you will:

  
  

* **Turn strategy into execution.** Translate Leadership Academy priorities into an integrated portfolio, implementation roadmap and operating plan.
* **Lead complex work from idea to impact.** Guide cross-functional initiatives from concept and design through implementation, evaluation and scale.
* **Build the Academy’s operating infrastructure.** Establish governance, decision points, roles, handoffs, planning processes and operating rhythms that create clarity and accountability.
* **Connect work across St. Jude.** Build strong partnerships across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and other institutional functions, bringing people and priorities together while maintaining clear roles and ownership.
* **See around corners.** Identify dependencies, duplication, capacity constraints, gaps and execution risks across the Academy’s portfolio and drive solutions.
* **Create visibility into impact.** Establish portfolio-level measures, dashboards and reporting that show progress, outcomes and organizational impact.
* **Help good ideas scale.** Develop practical approaches for moving promising concepts and pilots into sustainable institutional practices.
* **Lead operational and resource planning.** Oversee budgets, resources, technology, vendors, contracts and external partnerships that support the Academy’s work.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Apply human-centered design, agile and continuous-improvement approaches to strengthen programs, processes and operations.

As we continue to grow, we are seeking an experienced Director of Operations to provide strategic leadership, drive operational performance, & support the continued success of our store network.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Operations provides strategic leadership & operational oversight for a multi-region portfolio of stores. This role is responsible for driving business performance through operational excellence, financial accountability, talent development, customer experience, regulatory compliance, & growth initiatives. The Director partners closely with executive leadership to develop & execute company strategies while leading Regional Managers & field leadership teams in achieving organizational goals.

This position plays a key role in establishing operational standards, improving profitability, developing future leaders, & ensuring consistent execution across all locations. * Lead operational audits & corrective action programs to address compliance & performance gaps.

* Proven track record of driving sales growth, profitability improvement, & operational excellence.
* Strong background in P&L management, labor management, financial analysis, budgeting, & strategic planning.
* Experience leading organizational change, business transformation, & large-scale operational initiatives.
* Extensive knowledge of regulatory compliance, food safety, labor laws, & risk management.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, coaching, & team development skills.
* Advanced analytical, decision-making, & problem-solving abilities.
